titles.title: Paul's Kachina

credit_line: Gift of The Georgia O'Keeffe Foundation
description: In the Hopi culture, the term Katsina (Katsinam, plural), also Kachina, is only used in reference to spirit beings. The Hopi term for the carved wooden figures that represent the Katsinam is Katsina tihu (tithu, plural). Georgia O'Keeffe created paintings of Hopi katsina dolls (tithu) between 1931 and 1942. These religious figures were highly visible and available to non-Hopi and non-Pueblo people during this time, but the museum has no record regarding why she painted or drew these figures nor where she saw them.  The head of a kachina is the central focus of this round panel.  The head is painted yellow, and two orange shapes protrude from the head on each side.  Feathers extend from the top of the head and from behind on the left side.  Five cross marks in various colors also decorate the face.
